summary: Early throttling observed when many short-lived streaming sessions are opened via pooled proxies
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports repeated 429 errors while ingesting streaming requests from a parallelized uploader. The customer uses a client that opens many short-lived streaming sessions (0.5–3s) through a pooled HTTP/2 proxy fleet. The 429s appear within the first few seconds of a large fanout and are not correlated with sustained token usage per dashboard graphs.

Impact:
- NimbusSearch sees ~10–15% of streaming session starts fail with 429 during hourly import windows, causing retries and significant end-to-end latency for their customers.
- Affects production in us-east and intermittently in eu-west. Dedicated pool for the customer; they have a committed capacity contract but are seeing tenant-level throttles.

Environment:
- Customer tier: dedicated
- Region: us-east (primary), eu-west (failover)
- Integration: HTTP/2 multiplexed streaming via pooled proxies (third-party CDN-like proxy layer)
- Session pattern: many short-lived sessions created in parallel by workers (hundreds concurrently), each session may send only a few tokens before close.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Start 400 worker processes that each open a new HTTP/2 streaming session simultaneously through the proxy fleet.
2) Each session emits 1–10 tokens then closes.
3) Observe 429 responses for a subset of session starts within the first 5–20s.

Logs / headers observed by customer:
- X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000
- X-RateLimit-Remaining: 996 (varies)
- X-RateLimit-Reset: 30
- Response body: {"error": "rate_limit_exceeded", "details": "token_quota_exhausted"}
- Note: token counts reported by customer do not match the rate header depletion timing (they see very low token consumption).

Initial hypothesis:
- Short-lived sessions are triggering both session-init accounting and per-token accounting; the token+session composite accounting path may be double-counting or failing to apply short-session exemptions during burst windows.
- Proxy pooling re-uses client IPs and connection contexts which might be aggregating token/session counts incorrectly at the edge and causing tenant-level throttling.
- Healthchecks or background warmup requests from the pool may be inflating observed quota usage in the first-second window.

What we asked from customer:
- Representative HAR/logs from the proxy showing timing of CONNECT/STREAM opens and closes.
- Exact client SDK/HTTP stack versions and proxy vendor.
- Account/org id and example request ids/timestamps for 3 failed session starts (we requested to <support@redwood.com> with headers).
investigation_notes:
2026-03-10 10:05 - Support triage: verified customer logs and requested request-ids and cURL examples.
2026-03-10 13:40 - SRE reproduced variant in staging: recreated a short-session fanout using HTTP/2 connection reuse through local proxy pool. Observed early 429s when session-start rate > 250/s even though token consumption remained low.
2026-03-11 09:12 - Confirmed edge aggregator increments both 'session initiation' and 'per-token' counters atomically for new streams; however, the refill smoothing window is short and can cause transient tenant exhaustion when many sessions are created near-simultaneously.
2026-03-11 15:27 - Found proxy pooling behavior where multiple logical clients share a single upstream connection, which masked distinct client id headers and caused accounting to collapse onto a single bucket in the rate-limiter.
2026-03-12 08:03 - Engineering created a staging patch to add a short exemption window for sessions that close within 2s: these would only attribute session-init charges if the session actually emitted > N tokens. Patch PR linked.

- Debug dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streams/short-session-fanout?var=org=nimbussearch
- Edge logs slice: s3://redwood-logs/edge/2026-03-10/nimbus-fanout-slice.log
- Rate-limiter trace: https://jaeger.redwood.internal/trace/abcd-1234
comments: 2026-03-10 09:22 - Ana Park (Support): Thanks for the report. We see the 429s in your logs; can you share three failing request IDs and the proxy vendor? We've opened this as SUP-863999 and will escalate to SRE.

2026-03-10 11:48 - Customer (NimbusSearch): Provided failing request ids: req_20260310_1a, req_20260310_1b, req_20260310_1c. Proxy vendor: FastPool CDN, they use connection pooling and sticky upstream sockets.

2026-03-10 13:50 - Marcus Li (SRE): Reproduced a similar pattern in staging using a local FastPool-like proxy. Observed early 429s at ~280 concurrent starts/sec. Collecting traces and rate-limiter counters.

2026-03-11 10:05 - Marcus Li (SRE): Edge accounting increments both session-start and per-token counters immediately on stream open. Suspect double-penalty for short sessions. Creating patch to defer session-start charge for sessions that emit < 8 tokens within first 2s.

2026-03-11 16:12 - Customer (NimbusSearch): Thanks, we can try a client change to reuse sessions longer but would prefer a server-side mitigation since their worker model intentionally opens short sessions.

2026-03-12 08:10 - Marcus Li (SRE): Staging patch deployed to canary. Observed 70% reduction in early 429s in staging scenario. Need runbook and QA before prod rollout. Linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/594
resolution:
Workaround: Customer can increase session amortization (reuse persistent streaming sessions) to avoid short-session fanout while we implement server-side fix.

Permanent fix (in progress): We will roll out a rate-limiter change that defers session-init quota attribution for streams that close within a short threshold (configurable, default 2s / 8 tokens). The patch is in PR and is in canary as of 2026-03-12; planned prod rollout after QA on 2026-03-16.

Follow-ups:
- Add explicit metric for 'short-lived stream' counts per tenant for easier alerting.
- Update support runbook to check proxy pooling and client connection reuse when investigating early 429s.
- Notify customer timeline and confirm whether they prefer immediate prod rollback if they hit regressions.

Ticket status: In Progress - waiting on QA signoff and scheduled prod rollout window.
final_notes: This ticket focuses on composite quota accounting for short-lived streaming sessions in the presence of proxy connection pooling. The fix reduces false positives by only charging session-init quota when short-lived streams exceed a token threshold. Cross-team action: edge-proxy, rate-limiter, and SRE to coordinate rollout and post-deploy monitoring.
